steps.name: Janie
steps.text: ...Are all these people here to see me bear the standard? I'd better not slip up...

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: No, I need to triple-check after all.

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: Banner's brand new, no wrinkles, good. My clothes are prim and tidy, good. And my saber and boots... Alright, all polished clean, that's fine too.

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: Oh, right, my hair too! Oh, good, good, it's still neat.

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: The wind was gusting so hard just now... I wouldn't want to mess it up right here, not when I spent all of yesterday treating my hair. That would've been such a waste.

steps.name: Victorian Barracks Officer
steps.text: Now begins the flag-raising ceremony! All units, attention!

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: Phew...

steps.name: Victorian Barracks Officer
steps.text: Flag, forth!
Marching through the square, she feels the gaze of every soul in the crowd concentrate on her, and straightens her back even higher in response.
Hooking the ensign to the halyard, pinching a corner of the flag, she begins to await the signal.
Three, two, one, and the sound of drums finally quells. Quickly she throws the fly to the air, allowing it to unfurl in the wind of the morn. Thereupon, she hears applause behind her last and last.
Taking a deep breath, she pulls her posture tighter, straighter, but cannot help but let a smile slip from the corner of her mouth.

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: Wil, that's seven crates of pharmaceuticals total, all here.

steps.name: Medic Operator
steps.text: Thank you so much for running this trip, Janie... but it's funny, we paid for twelve at the caravan.

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: No, I know... they turned their entire hold upside down looking, but this seven's all they found, none more than that. And, well... they're not wanting to refund you the surplus money.

steps.name: Medic Operator
steps.text: But didn't we get the price settled all early this morning?

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: They lost a lot of freight coming here cutting through a combat zone, so they're insisting on ratcheting their prices up to cover the damages.

steps.name: Medic Operator
steps.text: But, Janie, we don't have much funds left.

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: Have resupplies from the landship still not made it?

steps.name: Medic Operator
steps.text: No... We haven't even had an update on them for the longest while now. Janie, you know, with all the turmoil at Londinium, you don't think the landship got...

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: Wil, stay with me. You said it yourself, times are turbulent. Odds are something's just held them up.

steps.name: Medic Operator
steps.text: So, then... what do we do now?

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: It's best we keep the patients' needs put first. Having these seven crates is better than none, and no matter how expensive, we've got no choice but to accept. Anything else... we'll have to make what savings we can.

steps.name: Medic Operator
steps.text: We can't just save our way out of this forever... All we've got left in the basement's some sprouting potatoes.

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: I'll keep thinking of what I can once we get back this evening. It's almost time I saw Mrs. Sheila—her chimney's blocked, I need to take a look at that.

steps.name: Medic Operator
steps.text: Do that. I'll head back to the office for now, then.

steps.name: Haggard Woman
steps.text: Miss Saileach, Miss Saileach!

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: Mrs. Sheila, what did you come out here for? Your health is... Let me help you back in.

steps.name: Haggard Woman
steps.text: The wind's going so hard today, best we take a seat inside. You were off leaving the moment you pulled out of the chimney—I didn't even get the chance to thank you proper.

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: Oh, it's—it's alright, I can't really stay long, there's people sick at the office.

steps.name: Haggard Woman
steps.text: Weather's been nipping lately—are you and Wil bundling up well enough? I've got a few dresses here you two could wear—they're getting on a bit, I know, but they're good nice ones.

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: Thank you, I appreciate it, Mrs. Sheila. Still, Vouivre don't catch colds that easily.

steps.name: Haggard Woman
steps.text: Ah! None of that, you can still wear it even if it's not to keep warm. Your clothes right now are getting to be patchwork with those repairs, and I've never seen you wear a thing else. Don't you go anywhere, now, I'll run back in and fetch them for you...

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: R—Really, it's fine! I'll be out of your hair as soon as, Miss!

steps.name: Thin Girl
steps.text: (Hushed) Da, look at that lady, her hair's so pretty...

steps.name: Lean Man
steps.text: (Hushed) Pah. Cloistered, that's what you call types like her. Can't live without her daily haircare...

steps.name: Lean Man
steps.text: On, now, Ema, stop gawking. Move, move. It's almost time for the hairdresser's.

steps.name: Thin Girl
steps.text: Da, can we not go...?

steps.name: Lean Man
steps.text: What?

steps.name: Thin Girl
steps.text: Pleaaase, Da, I—I want it like that lady, not so so long, just down to my shoulders.

steps.name: Lean Man
steps.text: Ema, don't you let her influence you! It's a massive company what sent her down—she's not here to live our ruddy life.

steps.name: Lean Man
steps.text: Your ma's sick and I'm looking after her for love-long and a half—when am I going to find the time to sort your hair if you let it grow out?!

steps.name: Thin Girl
steps.text: ...But I... I—I really really don't want a buzzcut...

steps.name: Lean Man
steps.text: For god's sakes, budge it! You don't want me to hit you now, do you, Ema?

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: Excuse me, sir, but if you're talking to children, talk to them. What are you raising your hand for?

spans.text: Excuse me, sir, but if you're talking to children,
What are you raising your hand for?

steps.name: Lean Man
steps.text: I... well...

steps.name: Thin Girl
steps.text: (She uncontrollably sobs.)

steps.name: Lean Man
steps.text: No, you... naughty kids, you see, I was just disciplining her a little, just... it's just a little discipline.

steps.name: Lean Man
steps.text: You shouldn't be bothering over us, madam, really, I'm sorry about that... excuse us if you will, excuse us.

spans.text: madam, really, I'm sorry about that... excuse us if you will, excuse us.

steps.name: Lean Man
steps.text: Alright, come on, Ema, we're off now.

steps.name: Haggard Woman
steps.text: Miss Saileach, I thought you'd up and gone already. Here's your clothes, and here's a little sack of flour we had left over. You take it, now.

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: That won't do... Mrs. Sheila, do you have enough food for yourself?

steps.name: Haggard Woman
steps.text: Course, course I do. My other half's eating soldier's meals on the front. It's just me eating dinner alone at home, fat chance I'll run out, don't you worry.

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: Thank you. Thank you, Miss.

steps.name: Victorian Barracks Officer
steps.text: Janie, how long have you been sitting here?

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: Sir! Tw—Two, maybe three hours?

steps.name: Victorian Barracks Officer
steps.text: What did you come so early for?

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: It's my first time raising the flag in the square today—I was so worked up, I couldn't sleep a wink last night, so eventually I imagined I'd just come here first thing and wait.

steps.name: Victorian Barracks Officer
steps.text: Oh? You certainly don't look like you spent all night awake.

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: ...I had to find something to do while I was waiting for the sun to come up.

steps.name: Victorian Barracks Officer
steps.text: Grmph. Fine of you. You do look quite beaming.

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: You flatter me, Sir, really. It's a guard of honor's duty to mind their appearance!

steps.name: Victorian Barracks Officer
steps.text: At ease, guard of honor, at ease. The sun's rising now—go and see that the flag flies too.

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: Y—Yes, Sir.

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: Phew...
Combing her silken hair behind her ear in the dawn breeze, the girl straightens herself and makes for the flagpole stood in the center of the square, the flag held in her hands.
As it gracefully ascends, enthusiastic claps come from the masses that have waited for this since the wee hours.
In all the applause, the girl catches a few sunken mutters.
It's queer business. Did they really have to send our town of County Hillock a whole dedicated guard of honor, just to raise a flag? It's like we haven't even a say in the matter.
Heh, I wouldn't crawl out of bed at daft o'clock just to watch Lord Snooty hoist a flag up. At least seeing this warms your cockles, nah?
If it were up to me, they would've sent us a few film posters instead. One for each of us to stick on our walls and admire every day—that's how you raise a spirit or two.

spans.text: If it were up to me, they would've sent us a few film posters instead. One for each of us to stick on our walls and admire every day—
how you raise a spirit or two.

steps.text: Ah, shut, don't you start. A guard of honor's what it is—isn't having a sight for sore eyes enough? What are you so greedy for?
Looking through the crowd, the girl attempts to pick out who's talking.
But each and every one of their faces brims with a lauding smile, and she has to wonder if those voices weren't just the wind talking.
The morning gusts blow bitter cold through the square all asudden, the air digging under her collar.
In the breeze, she cannot help but give a shiver.

steps.name: Medic Operator
steps.text: Get up! Janie, wakey-wakey!

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: Wil... what time is it?

steps.name: Medic Operator
steps.text: Gone five, but we're only off at six. You've got time to plait your braids.

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: No... don't mind that, I'm leaving it today. We can head off straight away.

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: Er... Wil, do you know where the hairdresser's is in this town? I'm thinking of getting my hair cut.

steps.name: Medic Operator
steps.text: Y—You what?!

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: If... If there's not one, I'm just as okay cutting it myself.

steps.name: Medic Operator
steps.text: No, not that... of course there's a hairdresser's here, it's the last house at the end of the street. But, Janie... your hair's so nice. The waste of lopping it off.

spans.text: No, not that... of course there's a hairdresser's here, it's the last house at the end of the street. But, Janie... your hair's so nice. The

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: It does tend to get in the way awfully at work, growing it out, see... Could you take over my shift tomorrow afternoon then?

steps.name: Medic Operator
steps.text: Whaa—what's the hurry? You're not gonna wait a little longer?

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: You don't want me cutting my hair short?

steps.name: Medic Operator
steps.text: I mean, it's fine, cut however short you feel... If it'll make work easier, plus I'm sure short hair would look just as fantastic on you.

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: ...Thank you for that, Wil.

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: Excuse me, are you open right now?

steps.name: Hairdresser
steps.text: Miss Saileach?

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: Do you know of me, sir?

steps.name: Hairdresser
steps.text: Who wouldn't in this town?

steps.name: Hairdresser
steps.text: What brings you here today? Hair treatment?

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: No, no, I'm here for a haircut.

steps.name: Hairdresser
steps.text: A haircut, then... Take a seat, Miss Saileach, I'll fetch the scissors. If you need a sip of water, it's on the table...

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: Thank you, sir.

steps.name: Hairdresser
steps.text: How short are you wanting it?

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: About to where everyone has it, please.

steps.name: Hairdresser
steps.text: Okay... I'll be starting, then, Miss Saileach?

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: Mm...
In the mirror, the hairdresser lifts a lock of the girl's hair between his fingers. Blade crosses blade, and in one go, the hair falls away from his hand.
The girl stares at the lock, fallen to the floor in a pile, and empties her mind, waiting for the scissors by her ears to snip a second time.
She waits a good moment, and it doesn't come.

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: Sir?

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: Why did you stop cutting?

steps.name: Hairdresser
steps.text: Miss Saileach, news doesn't get around our parts as well as it does yours. You're from some big old company, you've a million channels open to you versus us run-of-the-mill folk. I wanted to... to ask...

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: That's alright, sir. If you need it, then of course I'll help you. What did you want to inquire about?

steps.name: Hairdresser
steps.text: It's... no, it's not like that, I just wanted to ask—you lot see something out of sorts about the town, don't you?

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: What makes you wonder that...?

steps.name: Hairdresser
steps.text: Why don't you tell me, Miss Saileach? Here you've come to get a haircut.

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: It's—a haircut, is all it is, sir.

steps.name: Hairdresser
steps.text: Miss Saileach, isn't this the way you've always looked? What makes you want your hair short all of a sudden now?

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: I just... only have so much time and energy, I—I can't afford to mind this sort of thing...

steps.name: Hairdresser
steps.text: Something's about to happen, isn't it?

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: I—I haven't had any info of the sort suggest that. Everything seems... fine for the moment.

steps.name: Hairdresser
steps.text: No... that's lies you're telling, Miss Saileach. Be honest with me. Those Sarkaz are soon to come storming this way, aren't they?

steps.name: Hairdresser
steps.text: I suppose you think we'd all be crushed by the truth, so you're keeping quiet from us, zipping your lips. That's it, isn't it?

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: Sir, I haven't hidden a single thing from any of you!

steps.name: Hairdresser
steps.text: Okay... if things aren't turning for the worse, then why are you coming here for a haircut?!

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: Sir... don't get so worked up, please, can you—can you calm down?

steps.name: Hairdresser
steps.text: You show up at mine today out of nowhere, asking me to lop off your hair, and apparently the shorter the better—you sound to me like you plan to cark it and spend the whole next life not even giving a shake that hair grows on your head.

spans.text: You show up at mine today out of nowhere, asking me to lop off your hair, and apparently the shorter the better—you sound to me like you plan to cark it and spend the whole next life not even giving a
that hair grows on your head.

steps.name: Hairdresser
steps.text: No matter how miserable it's ever gotten, you've—you've never up and said you'd get a haircut, right, so what's making you get one today?

steps.name: Hairdresser
steps.text: I'm sorry, I...

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: I think I'd best find the time to come another day, sir.

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: Mrs. Sheila?

steps.name: Haggard Woman
steps.text: Miss Saileach? What brings you around?

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: Nothing, I just came because I wanted a haircut. Work's been busy lately, and I can't find the time to sort it all.

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: Wait... Mrs. Sheila, are you wearing lipstick today? No wonder you look like you've perked up. This red really suits you.
Saileach's praise doesn't seem to bring any delight to the woman, who hastily uses her own hand to wipe the carmine off her lips.
She then lifts a corner of her hem, and rubs the remaining dye from the back of her hand.
Her sheer vigor chafes the skin of her hand raw, yet the color just won't come fully clean.

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: Mrs. Sheila, wh—what are you...?

steps.name: Haggard Woman
steps.text: No, I was just going silly—as if this is any sort of time to be bringing out lipstick—when we've got even people living respectable lives like you losing the will to—... *sigh* This is awful.

steps.name: Haggard Woman
steps.text: If you'll... Miss Saileach, you'd better go on back to work, I'll—I'll just get myself home.

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: Mrs. Sheila...

steps.name: Medic Operator
steps.text: Hm? Janie, weren't you going for a haircut? I was looking forward to seeing your new style, you know?

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: I—I booked a new time with the hairdresser's. I'll go back in a few days.

steps.name: Medic Operator
steps.text: Good thing they didn't trim you, really, or you'd be hard-pressed putting this on.

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: A paper flower? Did you fold this?

steps.name: Medic Operator
steps.text: As if I'd have hands that skillful. No, a little girl brought it by—she said she hoped you'd like it.

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: It's so pretty. Folding a flower out of such a thin napkin must've been incredibly hard for her.

steps.name: Medic Operator
steps.text: Aren't you going to try it on and see? It must go great with your long hair.

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: I'm... getting it cut, soon enough... I'd just have gotten people's hopes up, wouldn't I?

steps.name: Medic Operator
steps.text: That's a few days from now, isn't it? Seize the moment, go on, wear it... Just put it on and see, look how nice it's folded and all—as pretty as any real flower.
She puts the paper flower up to her nose and gently sniffs. Through the girl's eyes flashes a hint of enchantment.

steps.name: Medic Operator
steps.text: Mmm... I think I can smell a flowery sort of scent from this... just vaguely...

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: Wil... it's not a real flower, no matter how much it resembles one...

steps.name: Medic Operator
steps.text: I know that, but it's almost winter, spring's a long ways away, and it's not like there's any real flowers about right now...

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: No one says you can't admire the flowers again in spring, now. Winter has its own demands to meet.

steps.name: Medic Operator
steps.text: But all that we do in winter's exactly so we can await next spring, you know.

steps.name: Medic Operator
steps.text: In the long, long midwinter, even a tiny little paper flower can remind us all, spring'll come on time.

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: And without that paper flower...?

steps.name: Medic Operator
steps.text: That I don't know, Janie... a paper flower's just a light in the dark, and no matter if we're with or without one, spring will come.

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: But even so, Wil, people are longing for the same thing. Not just that it'll come to visit them, but that it'll come in their hearts...

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: Maybe one won't live in winter forever, but one's heart can.

steps.name: Medic Operator
steps.text: True... true, that.

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: Phew...

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: You can hand me that flower... Wil.

steps.name: Medic Operator
steps.text: Oh... okay, okay!
Stroking its soft petals, Saileach pinches the paper flower in her fingers, gives it a few turns, then nestles it by her ear, and as if out of bashfulness, lightly lowers her head.
They're silent, for a while. Finally, she lifts her head, and looks her colleague in the eye.

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: What do you think?

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: Huff... so cold...

steps.name: Thin Girl
steps.text: Good—good morning, Miss Saileach.

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: G—Good morning, young miss, did you...?

steps.name: Thin Girl
steps.text: I folded that flower on your head yesterday... I'm—um, I'm really happy you're wearing it today...

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: Oh, this flower was from you? Thank you, it's very beautifully folded. I love it a lot.

steps.name: Thin Girl
steps.text: That's really amazing, thank you... Miss Saileach, can—can I touch your hair?

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: Of course, of course you can.

steps.name: Thin Girl
steps.text: Your hair's sooo so pretty. My ma used to have really long hair just like you, but they cut it off after she got sick...

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: I'm sure she can grow her hair out again once she's better, and when she does, it'll be even prettier than mine.

steps.name: Thin Girl
steps.text: Um, that's going to be a really really long time away, Ma's never... gotten any better... It's been making Da really sad.

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: Don't worry, you never know—once spring arrives next year, she might perk right up. Then you can take her to the park, and fold some real living flowers. I'm sure nestled in her long hair, they'll look wonderful.

steps.name: Thin Girl
steps.text: Nobody's hair grows that quickly...

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: That's okay, I'll come along with you then, and she can borrow some of mine...

steps.name: Thin Girl
steps.text: Borrow?
Saileach lifts up her hair, and lets it drape over the girl's head. A sea of golden blonde wraps around her, sheltering her.
A lock that falls into her hands is gripped, then once more let go.
Realizing how nervous the girl is, Saileach plucks the paper flower that adorns the side of her own head, and places it by the girl's ear.
In an instant, the girl flushes red.

steps.name: Thin Girl
steps.text: Am—am I pretty, Miss Saileach?

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: You are. You're very pretty.

steps.name: Hairdresser
steps.text: Ema, I'm done giving your daddy a trim, it's your turn now to... Oh, Miss Saileach... Can I help you two?

steps.name: Thin Girl
steps.text: Um... is that you, Da?
Seeing her father come out from behind the door, the flustered girl brushes Saileach's hair away from her head, and the white flower nestled in her ear is swept off onto the floor in her panic.
But unexpectedly, her father does no more than give her cheek a light caress, after which he picks the flower up, and puts it back safely in her hands.

steps.name: Lean Man
steps.text: Bet you got bored waiting. Cold?

steps.name: Thin Girl
steps.text: I wasn't bored! And I'm not cold.

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: Good morning, sir.

steps.name: Lean Man
steps.text: Good morning, Miss Saileach...

steps.name: Hairdresser
steps.text: Um... Miss Saileach... It's looking like I won't have time the next few days, so about your haircut, well... you'll probably have to wait a bit longer for that.

steps.name: Thin Girl
steps.text: Ah, Miss Saileach... are—are you cutting your hair?

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: No.

steps.name: Hairdresser
steps.text: You aren't?

steps.name: Saileach
steps.text: Yes, I've changed my mind...

steps.name: Hairdresser
steps.text: So, how about you, Ema...?

steps.name: Thin Girl
steps.text: Da... Can—can I keep my hair?
Through the avenue sweeps a gust of wind. Saileach combs the hair blown out of place back behind her ear, and looks at the man.
The girl grasps her paper flower tight. The hairdresser rubs the doorframe with the tip of his shoe.
Under all their expectant gazes, the man clears his throat, and finally answers.
